subject.title: Swarm unit atlas (9 brood variants + retinue), 8-direction - composite, generates nothing

sources.note: Brood variant 0 (state00_base). OWNER-NAMED variety source, 2026-07-29: 'the Oozes have some variance in appearence. They will be match to display weight.' One of the nine numbered states of PixelLab group 8b4b9811-dcf3-4e9d-baa6-2cb3f8901d0b, 88x88, 8 real rotations, low top-down. GENERATED NOTHING -- these were already on disk and measured (task-059 update I); this revision only reaches them. quantize is FALSE: the 4-value lock was superseded 2026-07-28 (docs/art/aesthetic-direction.md AMENDMENT, Emberkeep.Quantize 0). NO WALK ANIMATION: walk0/walk1 point at the same static rotation, so row 0 and row 1 are identical until an animate_character walk lands. The walk axis is kept anyway -- collapsing it would force a SECOND layout change the day a walk exists (task-059 update II). Which of the nine actually show up in play is docs/data/art/brood-variants.json's weight column, not this file: a skin that reads badly drops to weight 0 with no repack. brood1-sump is the look that shipped alone from 2026-07-28 to 2026-07-29 (it was RawArt/Renders/brood-ooze-colour, byte-identical to state01_sump), which is why it carries the heaviest default weight.

OWNER-SUPPLIED, replaces the 'unit-knight' Hallam sheet 2026-07-28 at the owner's direction ('lets reintroduce the color'): PixelLab character 243c7684-552a-4a73-9be7-046a8c5a9221, 8 rotations, 88x88, low top-down, one of 28 states in group 2cc3ab61-4230-4786-98fa-b94da9e99218. Authored in the web Character Creator, so like its predecessor this is an unmanaged path map -- no prompt or anchor of ours reproduces it. quantize is FALSE, unlike every retinue source before it: the 4-value lock was superseded the same day (docs/art/aesthetic-direction.md AMENDMENT 2026-07-28, Emberkeep.Quantize 0), so this sheet ships in full colour and the post-process no longer collapses it. NO WALK ANIMATION: this character has none generated, so south.walk0 and south.walk1 both point at the static south rotation. The other 7 directions already worked that way, but the outgoing knight DID have a real 2-frame south walk -- so the facing-the-camera view loses its leg motion until an animate_character walk is run and frames are mapped back in here. Deliberate: packing this cost 0 credits.

output.cell_note: 48 -> 56 on 2026-07-28. FORCED, not a preference: the incoming retinue character's content measures 41x49, one pixel taller than a 48px cell, and pixelpipe refuses to scale pixel art (correctly). The other two ways out were worse -- scaling destroys the art, and regenerating cannot reproduce a character authored in the web Character Creator. Safe because NOTHING IN C++ READS THIS: SwarmSheet knows Columns/Rows only (Mass/SwarmFragments.h), the material's SubUV split is the 8x4 grid and is ratio-based, and each request owns its own texture -- so this moves T_Swarm_2bit (448x224 then; 448x1120 since the 2026-07-29 rows 4->20 change, see frame_map_note) and nothing else. Visible consequence: a 49px sprite in a 56px cell fills 87% of the quad where a 46px sprite in a 48px cell filled 96%, so units draw ~9% smaller on screen. Answer that with Swarm.RetinueSize / BroodSize, not by scaling the art back up. ELVTR/SETUP-EDITOR.md:32 still documents the old 384x192 -- updated alongside this.
output.frame_map_note: Rows 4 -> 20 on 2026-07-29 (task-059). Row = Variant*2 + WalkFrame for the brood (rows 0-17, nine variants in state-number order), retinue on rows 18-19. THREE things have to agree about this grid and this is only one of them: SwarmSheet::Columns/Rows in ELVTR/Source/ELVTR/Mass/SwarmFragments.h, and the Niagara Sprite Renderer's Sub UV field on NS_Swarm (8 x 20). Change one, change all three, or the horde decodes garbage. Scripts/art/check_brood_variants.py fails if the first two drift. Rows are no longer a power of two: the repo's old 'Niagara needs power-of-two grids' rule is folklore -- the sprite renderer's Sub UV is a float ratio, so 20 rows decode exactly as well as 16, and rounding up to 32 would have cost 1.6MB of transparent texels.
